newsitem.title: USA: Vibe owners to buy rock magazine Spin.
newsitem.headline: Vibe owners to buy rock magazine Spin.

text.p: The investors who own the black music publication Vibe said Wednesday they bought the alternative rock magazine, Spin, in a deal valued at $42 million that could help cross-pollinate two musical styles.

New York-based Spin, the second largest music publication in the United States after Rolling Stone, will be owned by Vibe Ventures, which is backed by a private firm. One of the minority investors in Vibe Ventures is producer-composer Quincy Jones, who co-founded Vibe magazine in 1993.

Camouflage Associates said it sold Spin for $42 million. The closely held firm includes Spin editor and publisher Bob Guccione Jr., the estranged namesake son of the publisher of Penthouse magazine who founded Spin in 1985. It has a guaranteed circulation of 500,000, while Rolling Stone's is about 1.25 million. Vibe's is about 450,000.
"Music is one of the most powerful influences on young adults today," Jones said in a statement. "The prospect of these two magazines forming a definitive home for young adults is very exciting."

Guccione confirmed the sale figure and said his personal take was $16.5 million, from an initial $65,000 investment. The majority shareholder in Camouflage is businessman Stephen Swid, who will get $20 million from his initial investment of $6.3 million, Guccione said. The two minority investors in Camouflage are David Horowitz and Richard Keech.
Guccione, 41, said it was time to move on to new challenges, and that he would use his windfall to buy a magazine publisher with several titles. He had no particular targets in mind.
Guccione achieved some notoriety in 1991 when he was attacked in the Guns N'Roses song "Get in the Ring," along with several other writers and publications.
The catalyst for the deal was Bob Miller, a former Time Warner Inc. publishing executive, who owned a controlling stake in Vibe Ventures.

To conclude the Spin purchase, Miller approached Los Angeles-based equity capital firm Freeman Spogli & Co Inc. They formed Miller Publishing Group, which took a controlling interest in Vibe Ventures. Jones and his business partner David Saltzman are the other investors in Vibe Ventures.
Miller, who declined to discuss terms of the deal, said he has had his eye on Spin for several years.

"I think that Vibe and Spin both have a unique voice that speaks to that 18- to 29-year-old market. I think they're very, very compatible properties that we for a long time had felt would be really exciting to have under the same roof."
